options.text: Per-page fragments, plus `suspect_continuation` / `suspect_continues_next_page` flags
Per-page fragments with no signal — users merge downstream
Merge across pages in the document-level output
A deterministic `continuation_of` link in items

title: A cell holding a title and a paragraph
description: A bold underlined title over lines of explanation, in one ruled cell; two stacked values beside it.

options.text:
One row; title and text joined with `
`, values joined with `
`
One `<tr>` per printed line, the rule as written
One row; title bold, text after a space, values in one cell with a space

answer:
Answer: Keep one row for a single ruled prose cell. Preserve the title's emphasis and separate its paragraph with `
`; keep stacked values in the adjacent cell with `
`. Split only independently printed records into rows.

title: A cell cut by the page break
description: A long prose cell ends mid-sentence at the foot of one page and continues on the next.

options.text: Per-page fragments; the cell's text ends where the page ends, flag both pages
Per-page fragments, with the row repeated on the second page carrying the rest
Merge the two fragments of the row

answer: Answer: End the cell text at the page boundary. Put only the visible continuation in the next page's fragment and flag both fragments; do not repeat missing labels or values.

title: Repeating unlabelled record blocks
description: Blocks that repeat the same field set and print no heading of their own.

options.text: Derive headings — `### Vehicle 1`, `### Vehicle 2` *(current worker behaviour)*
Anonymous nested blocks — faithful, but hard to address
Flat in printed order, no grouping at all

answer: Answer: Keep repeating unlabelled field groups as anonymous groups in printed order. Use separate nested groups in items and blank lines between groups in Markdown. Do not invent `Vehicle 1` headings.

title: Where non-field text goes on a form page
description: Instructions, fine print, preambles. Always transcribed — the question is placement.

options.text: In place, between the key-value lines where it is printed
Gathered after the fields of its region

answer: Answer: Transcribe instructions, preambles and fine print in their printed reading position between the fields they accompany.

title: An entry with neither id nor label

options.text: A bare value (or bare `[___]`) — nothing else
Give it a positional id so it is addressable

answer: Answer: Emit an unlabelled value as a bare value, or `[___]` for an empty field. Do not invent a label or positional id.

title: A currency glyph printed before a blank
description: An empty cell or line that prints `$` and nothing else.

options.text: `$[___]` — the glyph is part of the blank
`[___]`, with `$` folded into the label
`$` as the cell's value — it is what is printed

answer: Answer: Keep the currency glyph immediately before the blank: $`[___]`. Preserve any printed spacing and leave the field label unchanged.

title: Blanks inside a sentence
description:
Affidavit prose with gaps: `The Enterprise is ______% Black Owned …`, `Executed on the (date) ___
day of (month) ___`. No label precedes the field; the sentence is the label. Hints inside the blank
and captions printed under the line are the same question.

options.text: Keep the sentence, `[___]` in place; a hint printed in the blank stays as text before it
One key-value line per blank, the key taken from the words before it
Keep the sentence and add a key-value line per blank after it

answer: Answer: Keep the sentence intact and replace each fill-in with `[___]` in place. Retain printed hints next to their own blank, once.

title: Checklists and boxes on headings
description: Items each led by a box, under a heading that has a box of its own.

options.text: Box-first lines nested under the heading, the heading's box first on its line
Label-first lines — `- **Item**: [ ]` — and the heading's box as a separate field
A plain task list, no bold, no nesting

answer: Answer: Put each checkbox before its printed label and nest the items under their group label. Keep a group-level checkbox on that group's line. Do not promote form labels to document headings.

title: An answer area printed as several ruled lines
description: Four ruled lines under one item number.

options.text: One `[___]` — one field
One `[___]` per printed line
One `[___]` plus a count of the lines

answer: Answer: Emit one `[___]` for one answer field, even when it offers several ruled writing lines. Emit separate blanks only for separately labelled or independently answerable fields.

options.text: Their text, as text, in reading order
A field with a blank for a reserved box
Nothing

title: A blank line used as a check mark
description: `___` before every item where a box would be.

options.text: `[ ]` — it is a checkbox by function
`[___]` — it is a blank by form

answer: Answer: Use `[ ]` or `[x]` for a short line functioning as a checklist control. Use `[___]` only when the line asks for a written value.

title: Values printed before the form is filled
description: `0 %` and `0.00` computed by the form itself in cells nobody has filled.

options.text: The printed value — `0.00`
`[___]` — the field is unfilled
The printed value, and flag the page

answer: Answer: Transcribe preprinted or computed values exactly, including 0 % and 0.00. Do not replace a visible value with a blank.

title: A label with nothing after it
description: `Signed:` and `Date:` with no line, box or space drawn.

options.text: `[___]` — the colon says a value is expected
Text — nothing printed says it is a field

answer: Answer: Use `[___]` after an empty entry label such as Signed: or Date: when the surrounding form clearly requests that value. Do not infer a field from a colon in ordinary prose.

title: Radio buttons
description: `[ ○ ] DENIED` / `[ ○ ] GRANTED` — pick-one circles beside pick-any boxes.

options.text: `[ ]` / `[x]` — the same as a checkbox
`( )` / `(x)` — a distinct mark for a pick-one control

answer: Answer: Encode radio controls as `[ ]` and `[x]`, preserving all options and their grouping. Keep any printed pick-one instruction.

title: Bars drawn in perspective
description: A 3-D bar has a front top edge and a back top edge at different axis heights.

options.text: Read the front top edge
Read the back top edge, where the bar meets the axis wall
Read the centre and widen the tolerance

answer: Answer: Copy printed bar values first. Otherwise read the value-bearing edge against the corresponding axis plane, excluding perspective depth. If the reference plane is ambiguous, estimate the midpoint of the plausible readings, widen tolerance to cover them, and flag the point.

title: A page with no ink at all
description: Not corrupt, not annotatable. Neither Ignore nor Reject fits.

options.text: Zero Blocks — the page exists in the sequence and is empty
One Block classed as empty, covering the page
Reject the page
Drop it from the document entirely

title: Pleading line numbers
description: Numbers 1–28 down the left margin of a court filing, with prose whose lines fall between them.

options.text: Drop the numbers; note once that the page is numbered pleading paper
A separate item listing the numbers, out of the reading flow
A two-column table, `number | text`
Prefix each line of prose with its number

title: Numbered section headings that read as a list
description: `1. AFFIDAVIT` over `1.1. COMPLETION AND SIGNATURE`, each with a paragraph beneath.

options.text: Headings, level from the numbering depth
An ordered list with the paragraph as continuation text
Plain paragraphs, number and heading on one line

title: Run-in headings
description: A bold clause number or glossary term starting its paragraph on the same line.

options.text: One paragraph, heading bold inline
A markdown heading on its own line, paragraph beneath
A `term | definition` table for the glossary shape

answer: Answer: Keep a run-in label and its following sentence, value or URL in one paragraph. Preserve printed emphasis; do not promote the label to a Markdown heading.

title: Stacked headings
description: A heading printed over two or three lines.

options.text: One heading, lines joined with a space
One heading per printed line, same level
Two levels — the first line a parent, the rest its child

answer: Answer: Join the wrapped lines of one title with spaces. Keep an article number with its title. Separate company names, exhibit labels and other furniture from the title; split title and subtitle only when the document establishes distinct roles.

options.text: One line per printed line, `Q`/`A` first, line numbers dropped
As a, with the line number kept
A `line | speaker | text` table
Prose, wrapped lines joined
Two blocks of lines, left then right, `§` and rules dropped
A two-column table
A key-value region
Row-by-row reading order

title: Stat tiles

options.text: Key-value lines under the panel heading
A one-row table
Prose

answer: Answer: Write one printed label–value pair per stat tile, in tile reading order, under any real panel heading. Keep units and qualifiers attached.

title: Slide section tabs
description: A row of tabs along the top edge with one highlighted.

options.text: All tabs, as a line of text
The highlighted tab only
Nothing

answer: Answer: Transcribe all printed navigation tabs in order as furniture. Preserve meaningful highlighting using the text-colour convention when it identifies the active section.

title: Decorative background art
description: A faint map or shape behind a slide's content, printing no text.

options.text: Nothing — it is decoration
A one-line description, out of the flow

answer: Answer: Omit purely decorative background art with no labels, values or meaningful relationships. Describe it when its geography or shape actually conveys content.

title: A line between bullets that is not a bullet
description: `partially offset by` on its own line inside a bulleted list.

options.text: A paragraph; the list ends and a new list starts after it
Indented continuation text inside the list

answer: Answer: Keep an unbulleted bridge such as partially offset by as a paragraph between the adjoining lists. Use indented continuation only when it belongs to one specific list item.

title: Bullet glyphs that carry meaning
description: `✓` bullets under Acceptable, `⊗` bullets under Unacceptable.

options.text: `*` bullets — the heading carries the meaning
`*` bullets with the glyph kept as the first token — `* ✓ Bank statement`
A bracketed tag as in [[Iconography and Symbols]] — `* [yes] Bank statement`

answer: Answer: Keep a meaningful printed bullet glyph as the first content token after the Markdown bullet, such as  ✓ Bank statement. Normalise only decorative bullet shapes.

title: A grid of equal blocks with no numbering
description: Nine address blocks, three by three, nothing numbered.

options.text: Row by row
Column by column

answer: Answer: Read an unnumbered grid of independent equal blocks row by row, left to right for a left-to-right page. Finish each block before the next; follow explicit numbering or continuation when present.

title: A page embedded in another page

options.text: One flat page: wrapper furniture, embedded content, both page numbers kept
The embedded page only
The embedded page as a nested block

answer: Answer: Transcribe the wrapper furniture, then the embedded page in its own reading order. Preserve both page numbers with their regions. Do not promote titles inside an embedded form screenshot into the wrapper's outline.

title: Marginal notes

options.text: After the paragraph they sit beside
Before it
Inline in brackets where the note's line starts
Gathered at the end of the page

answer: Answer: Place each marginal note immediately after the paragraph it annotates, as a separate block. If its attachment is uncertain, retain it separately and flag the page.

options.text: Describe as an image, keeping every printed label and dimension
Encode in FML or a similar floor-plan format
Both — description plus the structured form
Describe, keeping every component label and value
SchemDraw or an equivalent circuit DSL
Both

title: A data map with no printed key
description: The data-display test says table, but the readings are keyed only by coordinate.

options.text: Describe the map, transcribe the legend, do not attempt a table
Table keyed by coordinate
Both — description plus whatever table is recoverable
A `diagram` fenced block listing every label and its meaning
An image plus a prose description
Mermaid where the diagram is graph-shaped

title: Structural formulae

options.text: `mhchem` — `\ce{...}` for formulae, ions, reactions
`chemfig` — `\chemfig{...}` for 2D structures and rings
Whichever fits the specific figure, per page
Prose description

answer: Answer: Use `\ce{...}` for linear formulae, ions and reactions, and `\chemfig{...}` for drawn structures, rings and branches. Put standalone markup in a fenced latex block. Preserve legible structure; describe unreadable portions and flag them instead of guessing.

title: Printed staves
description: No convention at all today. Everything printed around the notation is transcribed either way.

options.text: ABC notation
LilyPond
MusicXML
Describe only — do not attempt to encode the notes

title: Logos
description: A wordmark in the corner of every slide, sometimes repeated faintly behind the content.

options.text: Its text only, in reading order
A bracketed marker carrying the text — `[logo: CIRSA]`
A prose description
Nothing — page furniture

title: Redactions

options.text: `[REDACTED]` once per blacked-out span
`[REDACTED]` plus the character count, where it is recoverable
A redaction item with a bounding box, in addition to the inline marker

answer: Answer: Write `[REDACTED]` once per contiguous redacted span. Keep visible text and any exemption code; do not infer hidden characters or their count. Use ordinary region coordinates when available.

options.text: Ignore colour entirely
Ignore decoration; record the nearest HTML colour name when colour carries meaning
Always record colour as an attribute on text items
Remove
A separate item, out of the reading flow
`<watermark>Redline Version</watermark>` in the markdown

title: A horizontal rule between sections

options.text: A dedicated JSON item, nothing in the text stream

answer: Answer: Emit `<hr/>` for a printed section separator in reading order. Reserve `---` for page boundaries; do not insert rules for whitespace alone.

options.text: A two-column table — `Label | Page`
A list
Whichever the litmus test gives on the page

title: Stamps vs watermarks
description: Both are page-level ink over content. Should they share one encoding?

options.text: One mechanism for both
Separate — a watermark is document metadata, a stamp is an act on this page

title: A total indented past its own children
description:
Apple prints `Total right-of-use assets` further right than `Operating leases` and
`Finance leases`, the rows it totals. The two rules then disagree:
Row-Label Hierarchy says count the absolute indent from the left edge, which makes the total a
level `2` — deeper than its children. Total and Subtotal Rows says the level records what the
row is the total of, which makes it `0`.
Following the indent produces exactly the silent double-counting that Row-Label Hierarchy exists
to prevent: a consumer reads the total as a leaf inside the group.

options.text: Absolute indent always — the mark on the page wins, even when it reads as a child
A total takes the level of the group it closes, whatever its indent
Indent normally, but never let a total sit deeper than the rows above it it summarises
Keep both — the indent as `data-level`, the closed group as a second attribute

default: **leave the row untagged**. No level is asserted where the two rules disagree
answer: Answer: Keep `data-level` tied to the printed absolute stub indentation, including an unusually indented total. Mark its label as th, leave values as td, and flag a contradictory grouping without changing the level.

title: `thead` / `tbody` / `tfoot`
description:
Quick Reference records that only `th` and `td` should appear, but that position was never
ratified — and the guide's own worked examples contain `<thead>` and `<tbody>`, because they
were lifted from this corpus. Over half the corpus contradicts a rule the guide does not itself
follow, which makes this a genuine open question rather than a defect to fix.

options.text: Forbid them — `th`/`td` and row order carry everything the sections would
Require them — the header/body split is real structure and should be explicit
Accept either, and say so — grading ignores the wrapper

answer: Answer: Accept valid `thead`, `tbody` and `tfoot` wrappers or their omission. Keep every row in printed order and decide th versus td per cell; do not move totals to a different position to fit a wrapper.

title: Rotated margin banners
description:
Text printed along the page edge — an archive stamp, a brand line, a firm mark — outside the
content, not across it.

options.text: Same as a watermark: once, out of the flow, `<watermark>` tag
Page furniture: transcribe as a page header or footer in reading order
Drop it as decoration
Depends on the words: metadata (a), branding (c)

answer: Answer: Transcribe rotated margin text once as a separate furniture block outside the body flow. Preserve its words, including branding; do not use a watermark tag unless the text actually overlays the content.

title: Drop caps
description: An enlarged sunk initial that the text layer separates from its word.

options.text: Join the letter to its word, no styling
Join and bold the letter
Verbatim from the text layer — `T he`

answer: Answer: Join a drop cap directly to the rest of its word with no extra space or special styling. Flag only a genuinely unreadable initial.

title: Where a displayed equation's number goes
description: `(1)` at the right margin of a display equation, cited in the prose.

options.text: After the closing delimiter, as text — `$$ … $$ (1)`
Inside the LaTeX — `\tag{1}`
Drop it

answer: Answer: Write displayed mathematics inside `$$` delimiters and put its printed equation number after the closing delimiter as plain text within the same formula block.

title: E-signature tags
description: A small coloured "SIGN" tab left in an exported form beside an unsigned field.

options.text: Ignore the tag; the field is `[___]`
Transcribe the tag's word where it sits
A bracketed marker — `[sign here]` — in the value position

answer: Answer: Keep an unsigned field as `[___]`. Transcribe a visible SIGN or INITIAL tag separately as an instruction beside the field, never as a signature or filled value.

title: Verse and deliberate line breaks
description: Poetry and other text whose line breaks carry meaning.

options.text: One newline per printed line, and accept that renderers join them

Two trailing spaces or `
` per line, so the break survives rendering
A fenced `text` block

title: Two strings printed over each other
description: A court filing stamp laid across a header the page already had.

options.text: Both strings, stamp first, each whole on its own line
Both strings in printed position, the stamp inline where it begins
The legible one only

answer: Answer: Transcribe each legible overprinted string whole in a separate block, stamp first at the overlap. Preserve readable fragments and flag any obscured characters rather than reconstructing them.

title: A signature whose name is printed beneath it
description: The glyphs are illegible; the name is printed directly under the line.

options.text: Bare `[signature]`, printed name as text — the rule as written
`[signature:K. B. Solanki]` — the printed name fills the tag
Both — the tag with the name, and the printed line as text

title: Seals and round stamps

options.text: The rim text as plain text where the seal sits
`[seal: …]` with the text
`[seal]` with no text
Nothing

answer: Answer: Use `[seal: printed text]` for a seal, preserving all legible rim and centre text in readable order. Keep it separate from body prose; use `[seal]` only when no text is legible and flag that limitation.

title: Line-end hyphenation
description: `Gov-` / `ernment` versus `air-` / `conditioning`.

options.text: Join soft breaks, keep real hyphens — a judgement per word
Verbatim, hyphen and line break kept
Verbatim hyphen, lines joined — `Co-lumbia`

answer: Answer: Join line-end word fragments and remove a purely typesetting hyphen. Keep lexical compound hyphens. When the distinction cannot be established, preserve the visible hyphen and flag the word.

title: Printed text that is markdown syntax
description: A line opening with `---`, a bracketed `[1]` that is not a form id, a `____` in a citation.

options.text: Backslash-escape every reserved character that would render
Verbatim, and accept the rendering
Substitute a look-alike that does not render

answer: Answer: Escape printed Markdown syntax only where it would change rendering, including line-leading `---` and literal brackets. Encode literal angle brackets as `<` and `>` when needed to prevent HTML interpretation.

title: Initials on every page
description: A handwritten paraph at the foot of each page, no printed line.

options.text: `[signature]` on every page where it appears
Once per document, out of the flow
Nothing

answer: Answer: Record `[signature]` on every page containing handwritten approval initials, including readable initials only when their glyphs support them. Keep the mark outside body sentences.

title: Redline in prose
description: Deleted text struck through, new text underlined, both red.

options.text: `~~deleted~~ <u>inserted</u>`, colour dropped
As a, plus the colour on each run
The inserted text only — the current version

answer: Answer: Preserve deleted text with `~~...~~` and inserted underlined text with `<u>...</u>`, over exactly the printed spans. Preserve colour as well when it distinguishes revisions or authors; do not infer insertion from colour alone.

title: A formula drawn as boxes
description: Boxed sums over a rule, an operator between them.

options.text: LaTeX in `$$ … $$`, the box labels as the operands
A `diagram` fenced block listing the boxes
Prose

answer: Answer: Write a boxed arithmetic formula in `$$`...`$$`, preserving printed operands, operators and labels. Use a diagram block instead when the boxes express a process rather than an equation.

title: A typed name on a signature line
description: `John North` typed in a plain face where a signature would go.

options.text: Plain text — it is typed
`[signature:John North]` — it stands for a signature

title: Small capitals

options.text: All capitals — what the glyphs show
Mixed case — what the text layer holds
An HTML span with `font-variant: small-caps`

answer: Answer: Transcribe the capital letterforms visible in small caps as uppercase letters. Do not add small-caps styling or silently substitute the text layer's mixed case.

title: Icons standing in for labels
description: A pin before an address, a handset before a phone number, a globe before a URL.

options.text: The values only, in order
A bracketed tag as label — `[address]`, `[phone]`, `[web]`
The nearest word — `Address:`, `Phone:`

answer: Answer: Use a bracketed semantic label such as [phone] or [address] when an icon clearly supplies the field label. Describe an unclear icon's shape instead of guessing its function.

title: Handwritten annotations

options.text: Plain text where the note sits
`[handwritten: …]`
Nothing

answer: Answer: Transcribe a marginal handwritten note as `[handwritten: legible words]` in a separate block near the content it annotates. Preserve visible fragments and flag unreadable portions.

title: Text clipped at the page edge

options.text: The visible fragment only
The completed word, when unambiguous
The fragment with a marker — `developmen[…]`

answer: Answer: Transcribe only visible characters at a clipped page edge. Keep the fragment and flag the clipping outside the text; do not complete the word or append an unprinted ellipsis.

title: A redaction that prints its exemption code
description: `(b)(5)` inside a box where eight bullets' text used to be; the bullet glyphs remain.

options.text: `[REDACTED]` once, the code dropped
`[REDACTED: (b)(5)]` — the code inside the marker
The code as printed text, no marker

answer: Answer: Use `[REDACTED: (b)(5)]` for a redacted region carrying that printed exemption code. Copy the code exactly, once, and keep unrelated nearby text outside the marker.

title: A structurally empty cell in a triangle
answer: Answer: c, with individual empty cells. Every row carries the full column count, padded with one `` per missing position — never a `colspan`/`rowspan` over the empty half, never an invented value. A deliberate carve-out from the free empty-region encoding in Blank and Spacer Rows: each empty position is a distinct coordinate, not one undifferentiated blank. → Triangles and Matrix Tables

title: Visually identical characters
answer:
Answer: a. Type the character you would normally use for that glyph; keep the visible form and
character count exact; never consult the text layer to break the tie. Grading is indifferent between
visually identical codepoints. This does not weaken image-first fidelity — where two codepoints are
indistinguishable there is no fact on the page for the image to be authoritative over.
→ Cell Text Fidelity

title: A cell whose only content is a coloured fill
answer: Answer: d. An empty `` carrying the colour — `` — using the nearest HTML colour name, never the legend's meaning. Same mechanism as highlighted text, so one vocabulary covers both. The mark is empty because the page printed no text; a consumer ignoring attributes sees an empty cell, which is truthful. → Color as the Value

title: Handwriting over a printed value
answer:
Answer: b, as `~~printed~~ handwritten`. Deliberately the same markup as a redline replacement —
a printed correction and a handwritten one are the same act, and the ink used to make the change is
not what a consumer needs to know. → Handwriting and Stamps

title: A stamp lying across several cells
answer:
Answer: c. Keep the text, emit it outside the table as page-level content — the same place a
watermark goes. Every candidate cell is equally arbitrary, which is the tell that the cell level is
the wrong level. Note this largely answers AMB-38 — stamps and watermarks now land in the same
place; what remains is only whether they carry the same tag. → Handwriting and Stamps

title: Markup for a struck value and its replacement
answer:
Answer: a. `~~1.316~~ 1.335` in one cell — both values, struck first, never merged. Matches
AMB-04, so a printed strikethrough and a handwritten correction share one encoding. The column-wide
re-read on finding a struck cell stands. Refined by AMB-07: the `~~` covers exactly the struck
glyphs. → Struck and Replaced Values

title: Suffix-only replacements
answer:
Answer: the strike span mirrors the printed strike exactly. `~~1.316~~ 335` when the whole value
is struck; `1.~~316~~ 335` when only the digits are. The unstruck prefix sits outside the `~~`
because that is where it sits on the page.
This dissolves the reconstruct-vs-drawn tension rather than picking a side: `1.~~316~~ 335` lets a
reader arrive at `1.335` without anyone having invented it, because the `1.` is genuinely printed
and genuinely unstruck. → Struck and Replaced Values

title: A grid printed inside a cell
answer:
Answer: subdivide the cell into the outer table's own grid — add the rows and columns the inner
grid needs, and `rowspan` the neighbours across them. No nested `<table>`, no flattening to text.
Both worked examples (`en`, `korean-curriculum`) are already encoded this way. A nested table would
hide the inner grid from anything walking the outer one — cell counts, column arithmetic and
per-cell grounding all stop at the `<td>` boundary. → Nested Tables

title: Marking a total row as different from a record
answer: Answer: d, plus `` on the label cell only. `Total234,846` The `` says the cell labels rather than reports; the absolute level says what it is the total of, so a grand total and a group subtotal are distinguishable without parsing the label text. General point recorded with it: a `` is a per-cell decision and need not span the whole row. A total row is part header, part data. → Total and Subtotal Rows

title: Header and body disagree on column count
answer: Answer: a — pad with empty cells. Individual ``, one per missing position, never a span across the gap and never a duplicated or invented value. An empty cell asserts nothing; a copied one asserts something false. Flag the page, since padding is a repair. → Header Body Column Count Mismatch

title: A footnote printed inside the ruled frame
answer:
Answer: b — caption text after the table, wherever the border falls. A deliberate exception to
the frame test: the line names no columns and carries no values, so calling it a row asserts
something false — a consumer counting records gets one too many. The frame decides titles and
banners; it does not decide footnotes. → Footnotes Inside the Frame

title: Where a caption goes in the output
answer:
Answer: follow the printed position — before the table if it sits above, after if it sits below.
Reading order decides it; moving a caption reorders the page. Attached to its table either way, and
emitted once. Explicitly not converted to a `##` heading, which would assert a document section
the page never printed.
Formatting preserved per run: fully italic, a bold label plus plain text, or a heading-like face
— transcribe what is printed and keep the boundary between runs. A caption set prominently is still
a caption. → Titles Banners Captions

title: Accounting numbers: verbatim only, or a normalised twin
answer:
Answer: a — verbatim only. No normalised twin in items, no per-mode switch. Normalising these is
a guess rather than a transformation: `$—` may be zero or not-applicable, `n/m` is neither null nor
empty, and `△2.5%` carries a conventional sign that is not printed. One value per cell, and it is
the one on the page. → Accounting Number Formats

title: How many blank rows of an empty pre-printed grid

options.text: Every printed empty row
A representative few
Headers only

answer:
Answer: a. Every printed empty row, however long the run. Trimming to a representative few is a
judgement a consumer cannot undo; ignoring rows they did not want is one they can.
→ Empty Pre-Printed Grids is now a rule

title: Icons that carry a value

options.text: A bracketed semantic tag — `[yes]`, `[no]`, `[locked]`, `[sun: full]`
The nearest emoji
A prose description of the icon
Standardise to Unicode first, emoji as fallback

answer:
Answer: a, settled together with AMB-39,
which asks the same question of the same page. The bracketed tag is the form; AMB-39 adds that a
repeated mark is transcribed once per mark.

title: Dot leader lines
answer:
Answer: a — remove them. Recorded as an explicit exception to verbatim transcription: a dot
leader is the one printed mark that carries no information. → Dot Leader Lines

title: Icons that are the value
description:
A plant guide prints a sun scale and a water scale as icons. The cells hold no text at all, so the
icon is the value. Marks and Symbols in Cells already forbids the emoji substitute, but it
never fixed the vocabulary that replaces it.

options.text: Keep the emoji — `☀️`, `💧`
A bracketed semantic token — `[water]`, repeated when the mark is repeated
A count or ordinal — `[water:2]`, `2`
Prose — `high water`

answer:
Answer: b. One droplet is `[water]`, two droplets are `[water][water]` — the mark is transcribed
once per printed mark, so the count that carries the meaning survives.

title: Borderless block: table or preformatted

options.text: Table when alignment holds down the whole block; preformatted when it breaks anywhere
Table whenever a header line exists
Always preformatted — never guess columns

answer: Answer: always a table. A whitespace-aligned block is annotated as a table whenever it has columns; the preformatted fallback is withdrawn. Read the tracks off the widest row and place every value in the track it sits in. → Borderless Whitespace Tables is now a rule

title: A too-wide table sliced into stacked blocks

options.text: One table per printed block, each keeping its repeated label column
Re-widen into one table by matching the repeated key
Same rule as [[Column Continuation]], whatever that is

answer: Answer: a. One table per printed block, each keeping its repeated label column. Never re-widen. → Horizontal Slicing is now a rule

title: A landscape table on a portrait page

options.text: Rotate and annotate in the table's own orientation
Annotate in page orientation

answer: Answer: a. Rotate and annotate in the table's own orientation. → Rotated and Diagonal Content

title: A diagonally split corner cell

options.text: One cell with a slash — `Region ╲ Year`
Split into two header cells, one per axis
Leave the corner blank and record both labels elsewhere

answer: Answer: a. One cell, `Region \ Year`, the top label first. → Rotated and Diagonal Content is now a rule

title: A header label wrapped inside a word
description:
`Distributio` over `n`. Header Wrap vs Real Tier says join fragments with a space, which
produces `Distributio n` — a word the page does not print.

options.text: Rejoin into the word — `Distribution`
Verbatim with a space, as the wrap rule says

Verbatim with `
` between the fragments

answer: Answer: a. Rejoin the word — `Distribution`. A wrap inside a word is joined with nothing (printed hyphens dropped); only a wrap between words gets a space. → Header Wrap vs Real Tier

title: Cells shaded to mean "not applicable"
description:
A grey fill over whole columns of a block, with no text. The fill is not a value; it marks cells
the schedule does not compute. Color as the Value covers a fill that is the value.

options.text: Empty `` — the shading is layout
An empty grey `<mark>` per cell, as for a colour value
A `colspan`/`rowspan` over the shaded region

answer: Answer: b. An empty grey `<mark>` per shaded cell, the same encoding as a colour value. The fill is what the page printed; never a span over the region. → Color as the Value

title: A total row with no label
description: Bold, ruled, closing the column — and the label cell is empty.

options.text: `<th></th>` — an empty heading cell, level as for a total
`` — an ordinary empty cell; the rule and bold are the only tells
`<th>Total</th>` — invent the label the page implies

answer: Answer: b. ``. Nothing is printed, so nothing is labelled and nothing is invented; the rule and the bold are transcribed as they print. → Total and Subtotal Rows

title: A numbered heading between fragments that share one header
description:
Note 20 and note 21 sit under one printed header. Split Tables Sharing a Header says a
paragraph in the gap does not break the table; a note heading is a stronger break.

options.text: One table, the heading as a band row
Two tables, the second repeating the header it depends on
Two tables, the second headerless

answer: Answer: a. One table; the note heading becomes a band row. → Split Tables Sharing a Header

title: Rows printed after a total that it does not include
description: `USA` and `Australia` follow `Total` at the same indent as the rows the total sums.

options.text: Same level as the components — the indent is what is printed
A level below the total's, so they read as outside the group
A separate table after the total

answer: Answer: one table. The memo rows stay in the same table, in printed order, at the level their indent prints. Never a second table. → Total and Subtotal Rows

title: A row label that wraps
description: A stub label over two lines, the value beside the second.

options.text: One row, label joined with a space
Two rows, as the one-`<tr>`-per-line rule says, the first with empty value cells

One row, label joined with `
`

answer: Answer: a. One row, the wrapped label joined with a space. The one-`<tr>`-per-line rule is for records, not for a label that wraps. → Record Groups and Multi-Line Cells

title: A total label printed in a different column
description: `ONEIDA Total` set across the boundary of the county and town columns, sum in the count column.

options.text: Label in the stub column, `<th>`, the town cell empty
Label in the column where it starts — the town column — stub empty
`<th colspan="2">` over both

answer: Answer: one stub column. County names and town names share a single column — the left/right alignment is styling — and the total label goes in it as a `<th>`. → Total and Subtotal Rows

title: A stub split into two columns
description: `– external` / `– intra-group` set in a second column beside their parent label.

options.text: Children at level 1 under the parent, the second column folded into the stub
A two-column stub: parent cell with rowspan, sub-label in its own column
Parent and sub-label joined into one label per row

answer: Answer: b. A two-column stub: the parent in the first column with a `rowspan` over its children, each sub-label in the second column on its own row. → Row-Label Hierarchy

title: A two-sided balance sheet in one frame
description: Assets, liabilities and an income statement side by side under one box.

options.text: Three tables, one per column block
Two tables — the balance sheet as one, the income statement as another
One table, row *n* across all blocks

answer: Answer: c. One table, row n across all blocks, exactly as the frame prints it. → Side-by-Side Mini Tables

title: A units row in the middle of the body

options.text: A band row — every cell a heading
Split the table there, the units line heading the second
Fold the units into the labels below it and drop the line

answer: Answer: a. A band row, every cell `<th>` — the `S$` cells included. → Units Row

title: Leader lines with two values at the end
description: `Name …… email  phone`, some lines without the e-mail.

options.text: A three-column table, leaders removed
Text lines, leaders removed, values separated by spaces
A two-column table, e-mail and phone in one cell

answer: Answer: b. Text lines, leaders removed, values separated by spaces. Not a table. → Dot Leader Lines

title: Values staggered inside one column
description: Parent totals at the column edge, children centred further left, all in one ruled column.

options.text: One value column; hierarchy only from the stub's `data-level`
Two value columns, one per printed alignment

answer: Answer: a. One value column; the hierarchy comes only from the stub's `data-level`. → Row-Label Hierarchy

title: The minus sign
description: `−742` set with U+2212.

options.text: Add U+2212 ≡ hyphen-minus to the accepted homoglyphs
Keep it distinct — a minus is a mark, not a dash

answer: Answer: normalise. Write the hyphen-minus `-` for a printed minus sign; U+2212 ≡ U+002D joins the accepted homoglyphs. → Cell Text Fidelity

title: A title printed in the corner cell
description: `Financial highlights` in the stub's header cell, the period tiers to its right.

options.text: It is the stub header — `<th>Financial highlights</th>` in the header row
It is the title — a caption, and the corner cell is empty
Both — the caption and the corner cell

answer: Answer: a. The corner text is the stub header — `<th>Financial highlights</th>` — and not a caption. → Titles Banners Captions

title: A progress-and-target bar
description: A single bar with a current value and a target on a 0→max axis.

options.text: Its own chart type
A one-row bar chart
A key-value pair — not a chart at all

answer: Answer: b. A one-row bar chart, emitting the current value, the target and the axis end-points. → Bars and Histograms

title: Annotations aligned to chart rows
description:
Each bar has one or two bullet lines printed beside it in a column to the right, naming
sub-businesses with their own growth figures.

options.text: Not chart data — a list, transcribed after the chart in reading order
Chart data — one rule per bullet, labelled by its bar's category
Both

answer: Answer: one table with a list column. The chart and its annotations are transcribed as one table, one row per bar, with a column holding each row's bullet lines as a list. → Stacked Bars and Waterfalls

title: A line break inside one printed block
description:
A masthead, address or banner printed on two lines is one block — that part is settled. What is
unsettled is which break to emit between the lines.
Whatever is chosen applies to every multi-line block — paragraphs, addresses, headers and footers
alike, not one spelling per kind.
→ Line Breaks Inside a Block

options.text: A plain newline. Renderers fold it into a space, so the lines run together for a reader.
Two trailing spaces then a newline. A real line break, but invisible in an editor and stripped by most whitespace normalisation.

`
`. Survives normalisation and matches what table cells already use; puts HTML in the Markdown.

title: Which output the annotation assumes
description:
Four situations have more than one correct annotation, and which is correct depends on what the
parse was asked to produce: whether the printed page number is recorded on its own, whether a saved
image may be referenced instead of described, and whether table fragments across a page break are
joined.
Option a is recoverable and b is not: a fused table cannot be split again if the setting
turns out to be off.
→ What the Run Was Asked to Produce

options.text: Annotate the narrower reading — fragments separate, graphics described, everything printed recorded. Valid under either setting.
Annotate the wider reading — fragments joined, graphics referenced. Unreachable when the setting is off.
Annotate both, and carry the pair.

default: the narrower reading, and flag any page where the choice actually bit.
